name: Exchange French (White)
intro: You are White. Your job: reach the Exchange setup — exd5, Nf3, Bd3, O-O, Re1 — then play the plans (Bg5, c3+Qc2, Nd2-f1-g3).

lines.line: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3 Bd6 Bd3 Ne7 O-O O-O Re1 Bg4 c3 Qd7 Nbd2 Ng6 Qc2

notes.1: French Defense. Your cue: play d4, then trade on d5 next move.
notes.3: Exchange structure reached — open e-file, symmetric pawns. Your kind of game.
notes.7: The ...Bg4 pin. Calmly prepare: c3, Qc2, and h3 when useful.
notes.9: Book almost done — from here it's plans, not moves: Qc2 battery at h7, knight to f1-g3.

lines.line: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3 Nf6 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O Re1 Bg4 Bg5 c6 Nbd2 Nbd7 c3 Qc7

notes.4: With ...Nf6 the knight can be pinned later — remember Bg5.
notes.8: Mirror pins: your Bg5 answers their Bg4. Keep developing.
notes.10: Book done. Middlegame plans: Qc2, h3 asking the bishop, rook to e-file.

lines.line: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3 Bg4 Be2 Bd6 O-O Ne7 Re1 O-O h3 Bh5 Bg5

notes.4: Early ...Bg4 pin: break it with Be2 first, castle, then h3.
notes.8: If the bishop retreats to h5, g4+Ne5 is always in the air. Book done.
